laser-1.situation_h2: You spent the summer taking care of everybody else.
laser-1.situation_body:
Camps, practices, rides, meals, somebody always needed something. For three months your day belonged to your kids. That’s the job and you did it.

The kids are back in school now, and there’s time in the middle of your day that nobody has claimed. Work and errands will take it if nothing else does. One hour of it could be yours.
laser-1.mission_h2: Spend one hour, three days a week, on getting stronger.
laser-1.mission_body: Here’s the objective, and it belongs to you, not to us. Three hours a week, on the calendar, while the kids are in school. Not to make up for the summer and not to get ready for anything. Just so you’re stronger, you move better, and you have something left at the end of the day for the people waiting at home. We handle the program, the coaching and the schedule. You show up.
mission_points: An hour of the day that’s yours
Energy left at the end of the day
laser-1.execution_h2: How the training actually works here
laser-1.execution_body: Classes run sixty minutes and a coach is on the floor the whole hour. The strength and conditioning is programmed in cycles and planned weeks ahead, not made up that morning. Every class is written at three levels, so somebody in their first month and somebody in their tenth year train in the same room and both get the right workout. We coach every rep. Six class times a day Monday through Friday, plus Saturday at 9:30.

execution_pillars.title: Everybody starts with Foundations
execution_pillars.body: Before your first group class you train one-on-one with a coach. You learn the movements, we set your baseline, and you find out how your body is working right now. One week and three sessions, or two weeks and six sessions. You pay for it one time and never again.

execution_pillars.title: Three levels, one floor
execution_pillars.body: Every class is written three ways. You do the version that fits the body you have today, in the same hour and the same room as everyone else. The program flexes so you don’t have to.

execution_pillars.title: A coach is watching you
execution_pillars.body: No leaderboard and no last one standing. We push when you’re ready for it and we pull you back when you’re getting ahead of yourself. You have people at home who need you healthy, so we train that way.

laser-1.consult_h2: What the free consult looks like, step by step
laser-1.consult_lead: Twenty minutes, free, and you stay in your street clothes. No workout, no weigh-in, nothing sprung on you at the end. Here’s exactly what happens.

consult_steps.title: 1. We sit down and talk
consult_steps.body: You tell us where you’re starting, what hurts, what you’ve tried before, and what you want back. We ask questions and we listen. Nobody here thinks you’re behind.

consult_steps.title: 2. We walk you through the gym
consult_steps.body: You see the floor, the equipment and the class times. We explain what Foundations covers and what a normal training week here looks like.

consult_steps.title: 3. You get the prices and you decide
consult_steps.body: We give you the numbers in writing and answer whatever’s left. If it fits, we book your Foundations right there. If it doesn’t, you leave with a straight answer and we don’t chase you.

laser-1.waiting_h2: What it costs to wait until January
laser-1.waiting_lead: This is the honest part. There are about twenty weeks between now and January 1st. That’s more than a third of the year. You can use them, or you can spend them and try to make it up with a resolution.

waiting_points.title: You stay the same
waiting_points.body: Twenty weeks is enough time to get noticeably stronger. It’s also enough time for nothing to change. Same body, same energy, same aches, and a new date on the calendar.

waiting_points.title: You start over in January with everyone else
waiting_points.body: January is full of people starting from zero. You could walk in that same week already four months in, coached, and knowing exactly what you’re doing.

waiting_points.title: You keep feeling like you’re falling behind
waiting_points.body: That feeling doesn’t come from a number on the scale. It comes from taking care of everyone else all year and never getting to yourself. Twenty weeks of training changes that. Twenty more weeks of thinking about it doesn’t.

laser-1.command_h2: Who you’re dealing with and where to find us
laser-1.command_body:
I’m Mike Manning. I own Black Iron Athletics and I coach here. I’m a Marine, I’ve been doing this in Frisco since 2013, and about 3,000 people have trained with us in that time. I have a two year old and a five year old at home, so I know what your summer looked like.

When you come in, you’re talking to me or one of my coaches, not a salesperson you’ll never see again. We’re at 279 Main St, Suite 122 in Frisco. Ask the hard questions and we’ll give you straight answers.
laser-1.faq_h2: Questions people ask before they book

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: Foundations is $360 for the one week, three session track, or $720 for the two week, six session track. That’s one time and you never pay it again. Membership after that is $200 a month for three classes a week, or $240 a month for unlimited, which includes open gym seven days. Military, first responders and teachers take 5% off.

faq.q: I haven’t trained in years. Is that a problem?
faq.a: That’s most of the people who walk in the door, and it’s the reason Foundations exists. You get one-on-one coaching before you’re ever in a group class, and every class is written at three levels, so you’re never trying to keep up with somebody who’s been here a decade.

faq.q: Am I locked into a contract?
faq.a: There’s a 90 day initial commitment, then month to month with 30 days notice. Ninety days is about how long it takes to feel the difference. After that you stay because you want to.

faq.q: Will the class times work with the school day?
faq.a: There are six coached class times a day Monday through Friday, plus Saturday at 9:30, and classes run sixty minutes. We’ll pull up the full schedule at your consult and find the one that fits between drop-off and pick-up.

faq.q: I can’t afford to get hurt. How do you handle that?
faq.a: Our job is to keep you training for decades, not to smoke you in week one. We coach every rep, we push when you’re ready and we pull you back when you’re getting ahead of yourself. Person first, athlete second.

laser-1.final_lead: Twenty minutes, free, no workout. You’ll leave knowing what Foundations covers, what training here costs, and whether this is the right gym for you. If it isn’t, we’ll tell you that too.

waiting_points.body: Twenty weeks from now it’s the same body, the same week, and the same plan to start soon. Waiting never feels like a decision, so it’s easy to keep making it.

waiting_points.title: You start over in January with everyone else
waiting_points.body: Start now and you’re four months in by New Year’s. Wait, and January is day one again, in the busiest month of the year, with more ground to cover than you have today.

waiting_points.title: You keep feeling like you’re falling behind
waiting_points.body: Every start that doesn’t hold makes the next one harder to believe in. That’s the real cost, and it’s the part we’re set up to fix.

shotgun-2.command_h2: Who you’re dealing with, and where to find us
shotgun-2.command_body:
I’m Mike Manning. I own Black Iron Athletics and I coach on the floor. I’m a Marine, we opened in 2013, and about 3,000 people have trained with us since. Plenty of them had started over more than once before they got here, and I’ve never thought that was a character problem. They were doing it alone.

We’re at 279 Main St, Suite 122 in Frisco, and the phone gets answered by somebody who works here. Come in for twenty minutes and talk to me. Worst case, you leave knowing more about your own training than you did this morning.
shotgun-2.faq_h2: What people ask before they start

faq.q: I’ve quit gyms before. Why would this one hold?
faq.a: Because the two things that were missing are the two things we do. Your training is programmed for you, so there’s nothing to figure out on a tired day. And a coach knows your name, so a missed week gets a text instead of silence. Most people don’t quit from lack of will. They quit from being on their own.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: Foundations is $360 for the one week, three session track, or $720 for the two week, six session track. That’s one time, never again. Membership is $200 a month for three classes a week, or $240 a month unlimited, which includes open gym seven days. Military, first responders and teachers get 5% off.

faq.q: I haven’t trained in years. Is that a problem?
faq.a: No, and it’s the most common thing we hear. Foundations exists for exactly this. One-on-one with a coach, no class to keep up with, nobody watching. Members are 16 and up and they’re everyday people with jobs.

faq.q: How much time does this actually take?
faq.a: Sixty minutes, door to door. Six coached class times a day Monday through Friday, plus Saturday at 9:30. Pick a time you can make on a busy week, not just a good one.

faq.q: What if I have to stop?
faq.a: Memberships start with 90 days, because real change takes longer than a month and we’d rather say that up front. After that it’s month to month, cancel with 30 days notice.

shotgun-2.final_lead: Twenty minutes with a coach, free, and a straight answer about whether this is the right place for you. That’s the entire ask.
shotgun-2.booking_sub: Twenty minutes with a coach, free. Grab the slot that fits your week and you’re done. 279 Main St, Suite 122, Frisco TX.

shotgun-2.rationale:
Real difference from shotgun-1: that page is the calendar and the arithmetic. This one is the restart cycle. Same twenty week situation, because that’s the stated situation for both shotgun pages, but here the twenty weeks are the setup and the honest part is why the last few attempts didn’t hold. The promise is a plan you didn’t write and a coach who notices, which is the one thing that page can offer that the calendar page can’t.

Editor’s cuts: added the twenty weeks into the situation so the page runs the brief’s stated S, which the draft had blurred into the restart story. Killed “Waiting never feels like a decision, and that’s exactly how it wins,” which is wordplay, and replaced it with the plain version. Cut “the two weeks of motivation” language down, cut “that’s the cycle we want to end for you,” and replaced the missing pricing question so Administration actually states the money before the cost of waiting sits under it. Consult steps are numbered to match the rest of the set.

The waiting section is empathy, not scolding. It hits the owner’s three beats in order and its hardest line is that every start that doesn’t hold makes the next one harder to believe in, which is true and is said as a friend, not a threat.

Shotgun rules held: no kids, no school, no family, nothing about a household anywhere, including the FAQ heading and the meta. Voice check: no em dashes, no emojis, no exclamation points, curly apostrophes, no banned words, CrossFit never named. Every heading stands alone. Facts exactly as supplied, and no phone number invented.
